items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: We didn't let a guy like Meyer Davis and them cats be, all them rich people looking for the Clef Club

ctx.x: Yeah, come to New York. Duke say

"You know what you're doing." I say, 'Man, New York's my town, don't worry about it. New York's my town." I knew Willie "the Lion" and Lucky and all them guys, and in the meantime I used to go there and rehearse every Sunday. I belonged to the Clef Club. That was big, that was big like the union is now. We had all the big jobs. / Wanamaker and all them people, had all them jobs. I was the youngest member in the Clef Club. We didn't let a guy like Meyer Davis and them cats be, all them rich people looking for the…

I'm 17 now, and anyway -- wait a minute -- anyway, we come to New York, so me and Duke had a room together. I had an aunt in New York, got a room. I think I was giving her about $3.00 a week. We had adjoining rooms for $3.00 a week, so me and Duke had adjoining rooms. Duke ain't never been to no New York. He ain't never seen no building as tall as that in his life.
